newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks expected to continue advance.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks expected to continue advance.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks are expected to power ahead this coming week after the blue chip Hang Seng Index last week jumped above the 13,000 point level for the first time since mid-March, analysts said.

A 94.72 point surge in the Dow industrials to 7,071.20 on Friday, following the U.S. April jobs report and an agreement to balance the U.S. budget, should trigger a strong rally in local share prices on Monday, analysts said.

"On Monday I think you can see the Hang Seng Index open almost 200 points higher," said Henry Lui, research analyst at Mansion House Research. Over the course of the week, he expected the Hang Seng Index to test 13,400 points.
The blue chip barometer jumped 435.94 points, or 3.45 percent, last week to close at 13,081.70 points on Friday.
Hong Kong stocks traded in London continued the upward move later on Friday, with the Hang Seng London Reference Index rising 181.96 points, or 1.39 percent, to 13,263.66.
"We are looking at continued bullishness next week," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities.
He also expected the Hang Seng Index to test 13,400 points.
Analysts said Friday's U.S. April employment report should soothe concerns about rising interest rates.
The jobless rate dropped to 4.9 percent from 5.2 percent in March but nonfarm payrolls rose by a lower-than-expected 142,000 and average hourly earnings declined.
"Fears of an interest rate hike have already subsided," said Alex Tang, head of research at Yamaichi International.
"It looks like the whole market will go a lot higher from the current level and probably we are going to see it move into the 13,500 and 14,000 area in the month of May," he said.
Analysts said investors were also expecting a pick-up in local property prices after a fall of about 10 percent since late March when the government moved to curb escalating prices.
"As long as the property market does not fall apart property counters should outperform," said Tang.

A strong performance in shares of HSBC Holdings Plc is also expected to continue. The stock soared HK$8.00, or 4.22 percent, last week, hitting a record high of HK$198.00 on Friday before closing at HK$197.50. "You will see HSBC breaking HK$200 in Hong Kong next week," said Rossiter.
But analysts said some red chip counters may see continued profit-taking this coming week after their recent surge.
Lui said with two H-share issues due to be launched in the coming week, some investors may take profits in some China plays and subscribe to the cheaper H-share issues.
Market sources expect Zhejiang Expressway Co Ltd and Beijing North Star Co Ltd to launch initial public offerings (IPO) of H-shares in Hong Kong from May 6 to May 9.
Red chips are Hong Kong-incorporated companies with financial backing from China and H-shares are stocks of mainland-incorporated companies listed in Hong Kong.

Shares of jewellery manufacturer and retailer Luk Fook Holdings (International) Ltd are due to begin trading on Tuesday. Analysts expect a firm debut but said worries over a lacklustre retail market may check the stock's gains.

Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd is due to release its results for the year to March 31, 1997 on Thursday. Analysts expected net profit growth of about 11 percent from 1995/96 net profit of HK$9.94 billion.
